title: Test Views with the Test Client
description: Write tests for list and detail views, checking status codes and content.
problemStatement:
## Your Mission

Assume you have a `Post` model and two views: `post_list` (url named 'post_list') and `post_detail` (url named 'post_detail', expects `pk`).

Write test methods in `tests.py`:
- `test_post_list_view`: should return 200 and contain the text "No posts yet" when no posts exist.
- `test_post_detail_view`: after creating a post, the detail view should return 200 and contain the post title.

Use the test client and `reverse` to generate URLs.
hints: Use `self.client.get(reverse('post_list'))` to get the list page.
Create a post in `setUp()` or inside the test.
expectedOutput: Running tests should pass, verifying view behavior.
solutionCode:
# blog/tests.py
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from .models import Post

class PostViewTest(TestCase):
    def test_post_list_view_empty(self):
        response = self.client.get(reverse('post_list'))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(response, "No posts yet")

    def test_post_detail_view(self):
        post = Post.objects.create(title='Detail Test', content='Hello')
        response = self.client.get(reverse('post_detail', args=[post.id]))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertContains(response, post.title)
